title: change-sentry: tie config/model changes to reference-corpus evals and governance
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: Model and config rollouts (kernel changes, quantization profile swaps, routing policy updates, new model variants) are deployed with insufficient automated checks against the canonical reference corpora. This causes silent quality regressions when small config changes alter output distributions.

Goal: Build a 'change-sentry' capability that automatically triggers a targeted eval suite against versioned, governed reference corpora whenever a model or serving config change is proposed or rolled out. The system should: 1) map a change to the minimal reference corpus and evals that exercise the changed codepath; 2) run lightweight smoke and heavier regression checks; 3) surface human-reviewable diffs and severity scores; and 4) enforce rollout guards (block/canary/auto-rollback) based on configurable thresholds and ACLs.

Scope: MD-> We will implement product-level orchestration, a reference-corpus registry API, a signing+versioning scheme for corpora, CI hooks for PRs, and a console UI for diffs and approvals. Infra work (autoscaling test runners, caching) will be scoped to a separate ENG sub-ticket.

Out-of-scope: end-to-end integration with Dedicated private control plane (handled later), broad rework of eval metric taxonomy (initial implementation uses current metrics baseline).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A reference-corpus registry API exists that allows creating, tagging, and revoking corpus snapshots with cryptographic fingerprints (SHA256).
A2: Change-sentry hook triggers on model/config PRs and on deploy events, and selects the appropriate corpus based on change metadata (model id, kernel group, quantization profile).
A3: Run matrix: smoke checks (fast) for immediate gating and a scheduled full regression run for detailed metrics. Smoke results must return within configurable N minutes (default 15).

A4: Console UI shows side-by-side aggregated metrics, distribution diffs, and example failing prompts with trace links to logs. Approver workflows (approve/reject/require-blocker) must be implemented with audit logs.
A5: ACLs: only users in the 'corpus-stewards' group can publish immutable snapshots; publishers can create signed drafts for review.
A6: Playbook: documented rollback criteria and automated rollback action through existing rollout service when a P0 regression is detected.
